# Disagreement Log — 1 Kings Chapter 19
**Reviewed by:** SOPHIA | **Date:** 2026-03-11

---

## Summary
13 verse(s) flagged for significant translation divergence.

### Verse 2
**EMET (literal):** And-Jezebel sent a-messenger to-Elijah, saying, "Thus may-the-gods do to-me and-thus may-they-add, if by-this time tomorrow I-do-not make your-life as-the-life-of one-of-them."

**LOGOS (formal):** Then Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah, saying, "So may the gods do to me and more also, if I do not make your life as the life of one of them by this time tomorrow."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah: "May the gods strike me dead if by this time tomorrow I haven't done to you what you did to them."

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 3
**EMET (literal):** And-he-saw, and-he-arose, and-went for-his-life, and-came to-Beer-sheba, that belongs-to-Judah, and-left his-servant there.

**LOGOS (formal):** Then he was afraid, and he arose and ran for his life and came to Beersheba, which belongs to Judah, and left his servant there.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Elijah was terrified. He ran for his life, all the way to Beersheba in Judah, where he left his servant behind.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 4
**EMET (literal):** And-he went into-the-wilderness a-day's journey, and-came and-sat under a-broom-bush, and-asked ʾet-his-soul to-die, and-said, "Enough! Now, YHWH, take my-life, for I-am-not better than-my-fathers."

**LOGOS (formal):** But he himself went a day's journey into the wilderness and came and sat down under a broom tree. And he asked that he might die, saying, "It is enough; now, O LORD, take away my life, for I am no better than my fathers."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Then he went a day's journey into the desert, sat down under a broom bush, and prayed to die. "I've had enough, LORD," he said. "Take my life. I'm no better than my ancestors."

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 5
**EMET (literal):** And-he-lay-down and-slept under a-broom-bush. And-behold — an-angel touching-him, and-said to-him, "Arise, eat."

**LOGOS (formal):** And he lay down and slept under a broom tree. And behold, an angel touched him and said to him, "Arise and eat."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He lay down under the bush and fell asleep. Suddenly an angel touched him and said, "Get up and eat."

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 10
**EMET (literal):** And-he-said, "I-have-been-very-zealous for-YHWH, the-God-of Hosts, for the-sons-of Israel have-forsaken your-covenant, ʾet-your-altars they-have-torn-down, and-ʾet-your-prophets they-have-killed with-the-sword. And-I-am-left, I alone, and-they-seek my-life to-take-it."

**LOGOS (formal):** He said, "I have been very jealous for the LORD, the God of hosts. For the people of Israel have forsaken your covenant, thrown down your altars, and killed your prophets with the sword, and I, even I only, am left, and they seek my life, to take it away."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He answered, "I have been absolutely devoted to the LORD God Almighty. The Israelites have abandoned your covenant, torn down your altars, and murdered your prophets. I am the only one left, and now they're trying to kill me too."

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 14
**EMET (literal):** And-he-said, "I-have-been-very-zealous for-YHWH, the-God-of Hosts, for the-sons-of Israel have-forsaken your-covenant, ʾet-your-altars they-have-torn-down, and-ʾet-your-prophets they-have-killed with-the-sword. And-I-am-left, I alone, and-they-seek my-life to-take-it."

**LOGOS (formal):** He said, "I have been very jealous for the LORD, the God of hosts. For the people of Israel have forsaken your covenant, thrown down your altars, and killed your prophets with the sword, and I, even I only, am left, and they seek my life, to take it away."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He gave the same answer: "I have been absolutely devoted to the LORD God Almighty. The Israelites have abandoned your covenant, torn down your altars, and murdered your prophets. I'm the only one left, and they're trying to kill me."

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 15
**EMET (literal):** And-YHWH said to-him, "Go, return on-your-way to the-wilderness-of Damascus. And-when-you-come, you-shall-anoint Hazael as-king over Aram.

**LOGOS (formal):** And the LORD said to him, "Go, return on your way to the wilderness of Damascus. And when you arrive, you shall anoint Hazael to be king over Syria.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The LORD told him, "Go back the way you came, through the desert to Damascus. When you get there, anoint Hazael as king of Aram.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 16
**EMET (literal):** And-ʾet-Jehu son-of Nimshi you-shall-anoint as-king over Israel. And-ʾet-Elisha son-of Shaphat, from-Abel-meholah, you-shall-anoint as-prophet in-your-place.

**LOGOS (formal):** And Jehu the son of Nimshi you shall anoint to be king over Israel, and Elisha the son of Shaphat of Abel-meholah you shall anoint to be prophet in your place.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Anoint Jehu son of Nimshi as king of Israel, and anoint Elisha son of Shaphat from Abel-meholah as the prophet who will succeed you.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 17
**EMET (literal):** And-it-shall-be — the-one-who-escapes from-the-sword-of Hazael, Jehu will-kill. And-the-one-who-escapes from-the-sword-of Jehu, Elisha will-kill.

**LOGOS (formal):** And the one who escapes from the sword of Hazael shall Jehu put to death, and the one who escapes from the sword of Jehu shall Elisha put to death.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Anyone who escapes Hazael's sword will be killed by Jehu, and anyone who escapes Jehu's sword will be killed by Elisha.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 18
**EMET (literal):** And-I-will-leave in-Israel seven thousand — all the-knees that have-not bowed to-the-Baal, and-every mouth that has-not kissed-him."

**LOGOS (formal):** Yet I will leave seven thousand in Israel, all the knees that have not bowed to Baal, and every mouth that has not kissed him."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** But I still have seven thousand in Israel — every knee that has not bowed to Baal and every mouth that has not kissed his image."

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

— SOPHIA
